question:
In the given circuit, if the input voltage lies between +E₁ and −E₂ , then output is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/153ddd24a7f8fc4701bbbdc01a3ea14526f63e27b98d4476e0cd015f06b18c0d.png] 

Input and output characteristics are shown below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/57ee1ba3e79a2e9477150b6dc83e5642c439b1b915c928b19bee93d6f36b7b74.png] 

The region between +E₁ and −E₂ is known as _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __Dead Zone__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dead zone__ is the region in a system where the output is zero despite changes in the input.
 
• In the given circuit, the output remains zero if the input voltage lies between +E1 and −E2.
 
• The system does not respond to minor variations in input within this range.
 
• It is a common characteristic in systems to filter out noise or minor fluctuations.
 
• The dead zone ensures stability and eliminates unnecessary responses to small changes in input.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Zone:**
 
 
• The region where the circuit operates linearly and amplifies the input signal.
 
• It is outside the dead zone in this specific scenario.
 
 
 
• **Cut-Off Zone:**
 
 
• This occurs when the circuit is completely turned off or non-conducting.
 
• It is generally observed in transistor-based circuits beyond a certain input range.
 
 
 
• **Saturation Zone:**
 
 
• The region where the circuit operates at its maximum output regardless of further increases in input.
 
• Saturation typically occurs when the input exceeds a specific threshold.
